question: secret
answer:
The benchmark keeps the NVIDIA API key out of its result schema and redacts it from errors and successful model output. There’s one gap in the failed-stream path, so this falls short of a guarantee.

- `Settings.from_env()` reads `NVIDIA_API_KEY` from the environment, optionally populated by `.env`. The benchmark passes it to the NVIDIA `Endpoint`, which sends it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Both dataclasses hide the key from `repr`. [src/nvidia_ai/config.py](src/nvidia_ai/config.py#L25) · [src/nvidia_ai/bench.py](src/nvidia_ai/bench.py#L379) · [src/nvidia_ai/llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L38)
- The writer serializes `ChatResult` fields and selected benchmark metadata. The credential-bearing settings, endpoint, and request headers stay outside that data. `redact()` replaces the exact key and token-shaped strings with `***`. It runs on error messages before truncation and on successful output and reasoning before serialization. A test checks that a 401 response echoing the credential is scrubbed. [src/nvidia_ai/bench.py](src/nvidia_ai/bench.py#L205) · [src/nvidia_ai/bench.py](src/nvidia_ai/bench.py#L345) · [src/nvidia_ai/llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L21) · [src/nvidia_ai/llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L127) · [tests/test_llm.py](tests/test_llm.py#L88)
- If a stream emits partial content or reasoning and then fails, `fail()` scrubs only the error message. The partial text can reach `results.jsonl` without redaction. [src/nvidia_ai/llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L177) · [src/nvidia_ai/bench.py](src/nvidia_ai/bench.py#L345)
